These cases should be left to the court of law, and not the schools. And actually, that's how things used to work 5 years ago. However something happened in 2011 changed this.

In 2011, Obama decided to address the sexual assault statistics on college campuses and created a list of "suggestions" that colleges must adhere to when it comes to dealing with sexual assault. To really make sure the schools take the "suggestions" seriously, he invoked "Title IX" of education amendment originally intended to ensure equal opportunity for women in collegiate sports. With Department of Education enforcement, schools that violated the "suggestions" would then violate Title IX, and therefore would have DoE funding taken away. Obviously this scared the shit out of schools, and since the "suggestions" put the school as the responsible party, colleges all over the US began taking on campus sexual assaults all on their own. Here's a few tidbits from the "suggestions" that explain why colleges have botched these cases:

Schools should use a "preponderance of evidence" standard to determine whether another student is responsible for an assault. That means that if it's more than likely that sexual violence occurred, there should be punishment.

Even if a student is said to have assaulted another student in off-campus housing, the school must investigate.

A school should not wait for the conclusion of a criminal investigation or criminal proceeding to begin its own Title IX investigation.

A criminal investigation is intended to determine whether an individual violated criminal law; and, if at the conclusion of the investigation, the individual is tried and found guilty, the individual may be imprisoned or subject to criminal penalties...By contrast, a Title IX investigation will never result in incarceration of an individual and, therefore, the same procedural protections and legal standards are not required.

If a school uses a hearing process to determine responsibility for acts of sexual violence, OCR does not require that the school allow a complainant to be present for the entire hearing;

For more information: http://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2011/04/04/135109643/colleges-universities-told-to-do-more-to-prevent-sexual-assaults

The complete document, 2014 edition (yes they even updated it): http://www2.ed.gov/about/offices/list/ocr/docs/qa-201404-title-ix.pdf

"It was also already said, but LoL represents everything that is flawed in video games."

As an avid League player I take offense to that and ask for your reasoning.

"Everything"? I can understand the high difficulty curve (Faster Than Light, anyone?) and the community issues, but saying it's the worst game of our time?...

It's not pay-to-win, doesn't have necessary DLC to buy to keep you on a competitive level. Hell, the game is free. Unless that's considered a flaw, in which case you're right.

Ah well I guess I was a bit extreme, didn't mean to offend, and in the end it is just my opinion. But I see games as art, and take a very literal definition of that, whereas games like LoL take games as sport. I feel this attitude is largely responsible for the lack of plot and the monetization of the industry. If you aren't making a game that can compare to Poe or Orwell and the like thematically in the way Dark Sould or Fallout can, then you're kind of just clicking buttons for shits and giggles, which isn't a bad thing, I don't mean to discredit fun. But the fact that not only people see the games themselves as money makers, but the whole "pro gaming"as a cash cow has in my opinion directed games towards simplicity. Even games that used to have "pro" fields would try to have artistic value in plots, but they don't even try in most cases anymore. Like Halo, even if most of Halo is just shooting people on the same levels over and over, they tried to insert critiques of blind faith into the story in the beginning of the series. And that had a fair MLG crowd back in the day, while still having a pretty open community, whereas Lol breeds a very toxic vibe. You could even see the artists attempting to make statements on the nature of the universe in something as light as Katamari. But that doesn't happen as much anymore in video games.

Which isn't to say something like Lol can't be valued in an artistic way, combat balance is in of itself a way to convey something or can simply be beautiful. My main issue it the attitude it creates and the standards it produces for games as a whole.

I understand your points, but I don't think the fault is with games like LoL.

For example: Pong, Galaga, Donkey Kong, Frogger, Pac Man, and Dig Dug. These were all extremely popular games, and they shaped the gaming community for decades. None of them tell stories, incite debate, or provoke philosophical inquiry. And yet, we get games like The Last of Us, Half-Life, and my personal favorite, Mass Effect.

Similarly, we get games like League and DOTA. No, they don't tell stories; no, they don't incite philosophical debate; and no, they aren't smart. This, however, does not impede other games like The Wolf Among Us from cropping up.

I think the real reason there are much more dumb cash-ins compared to smart, artistic games is because it's much easier to develop games nowadays. The average person can educate themselves and build their own game--it no longer requires multi-million dollar teams with dedicated artists, writers, and coders.

For example, Scott Cawthon. He single-handedly produced four horror games in eleven months. Meanwhile, it takes BioWare about five years to produce something like Mass Effect Andromeda.

When a mods become inactive a sub can be claimed by almost anyone. As a way for moderators to gracefully step down and to ensure takeovers are done with good intentions we should be able to Archive a sub preserving the posts and allowing someone to reclaim the name.

How it will work
When an admin or subverse owner archives a sub the following happen:

  • The subverse name is freed up to be taken again.
  • Custom styles and sidebar are removed.
  • All moderators, subscriptions, sets are removed.
  • Links to posts continue to work but no longer show up on /v/all
  • If the subverse is not re-created the subverse not found page redirects to /archive/[subverse]
  • If the subverse has been re-created a new archive tab is shown next to Top
  • Archived posts show up in general search but the subverse is name (archived)[subverse] and links to /archive/[subverse]
  • Archived post do not show up when searching within a subverse unless a search within archive option is checked
  • Voating, commenting is disabled within archvies.
  • Moderating archives are limited to admins.
Archiving a subverse; preserving old posts but clearing subscriptions and front page.
